title: Anthropic Hits $965B, Token Shock Bites Uber, Groq Pivots to Inference
summary: Anthropic closed a $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion valuation — surpassing OpenAI to become the world's most valuable AI startup — while simultaneously shipping a new flagship model that leads most industry benchmarks. On the deployment front, AWS launched an Agentic Shopping Assistant claiming conversion rates 3.5 times higher than keyword search, grounded in infrastructure built for Amazon's own 300 million AI-shopping users. Next week, watch Anthropic's IPO timeline signals and the FinOps X conference in San Diego, where token economics and AI budget governance will dominate the agenda.

Your Weekly AI Press Review — Week of May 30, 2026: Agentic Surge.

This Friday, Anthropic rewrote the AI funding record books — a $65 billion raise at a $965 billion valuation — and that's just the headline. In this episode: Friday's biggest AI moves through the NYSE close, the deployments reshaping enterprise workflows, and the week ahead. Stay for the off-radar segment — there's a governance time-bomb in agentic systems that almost nobody is talking about.

Anthropic closed its Series H this Friday at a $965 billion post-money valuation — the largest private AI funding round ever recorded. The $65 billion raise was co-led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron joined as strategic infrastructure partners. Fifteen billion of the total reflects previously committed hyperscaler capital, including $5 billion from Amazon. Run-rate revenue crossed $47 billion earlier this month — up from $30 billion in April and $14 billion in February. That trajectory has no modern precedent in enterprise software.

Alongside the fundraise, Anthropic shipped its new flagship model. The release tops most major benchmarks — including agentic coding, where it scores 69 percent on SWE-Bench Pro, versus 58 percent for OpenAI's latest. On multidisciplinary reasoning, it hits nearly 58 percent with tools — the highest in the field. The model also catches its own coding errors roughly four times more often than its predecessor. API pricing holds flat at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output. Dynamic workflows can now spin up hundreds of parallel sub-agents for tasks like codebase-wide migrations.

Groq is raising $650 million from existing investors, per Axios, as it pivots from chip hardware toward an inference cloud business. The raise follows a December deal with Nvidia — reported at $20 billion — that involved technology licensing and the departure of senior Groq staff. Backers Disruptive and Infinitium have agreed to fill the round if other investors pass on their pro-rata. Interim CEO Adam Winter and CFO Matt Eng are leading the new direction. Inference — the compute that runs after a prompt — is now the dominant AI workload, and Groq is betting its homegrown chip gives it a cost edge in that market.

Uber burned through its entire 2026 AI budget by April. CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga told The Information the company was back to the drawing board. COO Andrew Macdonald said the productivity link hadn't closed — quote: 'It's very hard to draw a line between one of those stats and 25 percent more useful consumer features.' CEO Dara Khosrowshahi confirmed agents built roughly 10 percent of committed code. Uber's R&D spend hit $3.4 billion in 2025, up 9 percent. The tools are working. The ROI math is not.

Microsoft canceled most internal Claude Code licenses in mid-May, redirecting engineers in its Experiences and Devices division to GitHub Copilot by June 30. Six months earlier, Microsoft had opened Claude Code access to thousands of employees. The cancellation doesn't affect Microsoft's broader Foundry deal with Anthropic, which includes up to $5 billion in investment. The pattern is the same as Uber's — token-based consumption broke the CFO's cost model. Annual seat licenses gave finance teams predictability. Per-token billing does not.

OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework this Friday, mapping its internal risk controls to the EU's General-Purpose AI Code of Practice and California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act. The framework defines systemic risk as any scenario causing more than 50 fatalities or $1 billion in property damage from a single incident. It introduces tiered threat categories across cyber offense, CBRN risks, and loss of control. OpenAI also endorsed Illinois Senate Bill 315 — the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act — which passed the state House on Wednesday and requires annual third-party audits and transparency reports before frontier model deployment.

Illinois Governor JB Pritzker vowed this Friday to sign SB 315 into law. The bill mandates frontier AI developers to publish governance frameworks, report critical safety incidents, and provide whistleblower protections. OpenAI called it a thoughtful approach and noted that Illinois, New York, and California are converging on a de facto national framework. For enterprise compliance teams, that convergence matters more than any single state law — it signals the cost of non-compliance is about to become a line item in every AI deployment budget.

A new review paper from researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Meta, and Stanford — published Friday — argues that the real bottleneck for autonomous AI agents is not the language model but the software layer wrapped around it. The authors call this layer the 'harness.' It covers tools, sandboxed environments, memory, permission boundaries, and feedback channels. DeepSeek is already building a dedicated harness team in Beijing. The paper's core formula: model plus harness equals AI agent. Without the harness, a model is stateless. With it, it can grind through multi-step tasks continuously.

IBM and Artificial Analysis launched ITBench-AA this week — the first benchmark for agentic enterprise IT tasks, starting with Kubernetes incident response. Every frontier model scored below 50 percent. The top performer hit 47 percent. GPT-5.5 averaged 31 turns per task at 46 percent accuracy. Gemini averaged 83 turns at just 30 percent — more investigation, worse results. The benchmark covers 59 SRE tasks, 19 of them held out. For enterprise buyers evaluating AI for IT operations, this is the clearest signal yet that current models are not production-ready for autonomous infrastructure management.

Box founder Aaron Levie coined a term this Friday that's already circulating in enterprise circles: 'AI psychosis.' His argument — the executives deciding AI can replace jobs are the ones least likely to understand what those jobs involve. ClickUp cut 22 percent of its workforce for AI agents. Tech layoffs in 2026 are already nearly matching all of 2025. DuckDuckGo mobile installs spiked 30 percent on a single day during the Memorial Day weekend — users reacting to Google's aggressive AI-first search overhaul. The backlash is real, even if DuckDuckGo holds less than 2 percent of the US search market.

Spain's government approved a draft Organic Law on AI governance this Friday, adding to a growing stack of national-level regulation outside the US. The law covers proper use and governance of AI systems across public and private sectors. Combined with Illinois SB 315 and the EU's General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, enterprise legal teams now face at least three distinct compliance frameworks — each with different audit, transparency, and incident-reporting requirements. The cost of maintaining separate compliance postures across jurisdictions is becoming a material budget line.

Tencent Cloud launched WorkBuddy globally this Friday — a productivity AI agent that connects to Slack, Telegram, Discord, WeChat, GitHub, Jira, Google Drive, and Gmail through MCP. The product includes more than 100 built-in expert roles and supports model integration via API keys. WorkBuddy was first deployed in China before this global rollout. It's a direct play for the enterprise workflow market that Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini currently dominate. Tencent's MCP-native architecture means it can plug into existing enterprise tool stacks without requiring a platform migration.

iFlytek unveiled 40-gram AI glasses at BEYOND Expo 2026 in Macau this Friday. The device supports real-time translation across 122 languages and uses a 5-plus-1 microphone array combined with lip-motion recognition to isolate a target speaker based on the user's line of sight. The company calls the feature 'hear who you look at.' The glasses target four use cases: translation, interaction, office productivity, and wearable comfort. iFlytek is positioning the product against Meta's Ray-Ban AI glasses and XREAL's AR platform — both of which are competing for what XREAL's CEO called an 'iPhone moment' for AI wearables.

The Lenovo Innovation Accelerator showcased nine hard-tech startups at BEYOND Expo 2026 this Friday, including Om AI Technology, SpacemiT, and AutoArk. The cohort spans RISC-V AI chips, AI creative workstations, AI glasses, and next-generation cooling solutions. Lenovo's accelerator model differs from traditional VC — it emphasizes supply chain integration and global sales channel access over financial returns alone. For enterprise hardware buyers, the signal is that China's AI edge-device ecosystem is maturing faster than Western coverage suggests, with commercial deployment timelines measured in months, not years.

The FinOps discipline has been transformed by AI spending. Two years ago, 31 percent of FinOps teams managed AI costs. Today, 98 percent do, per the State of FinOps 2026 Report. Ninety percent now manage SaaS spend, up from 65 percent in 2025. Sixty-four percent manage licensing, up 15 points. The Uber and Microsoft token-shock stories are not outliers — they're the leading edge of a structural problem. Token-based consumption breaks annual budget cycles. Engineering decisions now carry direct balance-sheet consequences that most finance teams were not built to track.

Sequoia Capital has quantified the AI services opportunity: for every dollar companies spend on software, they spend roughly six on services. A new generation of AI companies is skipping the tool sale entirely — deploying autonomous agents to run back-office finance, insurance brokerage, legal drafting, and revenue cycle operations. Gartner projects that 40 percent of enterprise applications will embed AI agents by end of 2026, up from 5 percent in 2025. The contracts governing these deployments increasingly resemble managed services agreements — priced by transactions processed or percentage of savings generated, not by seat or uptime.

Liquid's Co-Invest app launched this Friday embedded directly inside ChatGPT and Claude, letting users fund accounts, analyze markets, and place live trades without leaving the conversation. The app covers more than 500 markets — crypto, equities, FX, Polymarket prediction positions, and pre-IPO secondaries. Users set stop-loss and take-profit levels inside the chat. Liquid operates non-custodially. Robinhood's Agentic Trading and Agentic Credit Card, MoonPay's ChatGPT crypto integration, and OpenAI's Plaid-connected personal finance tools all launched in the same window. AI assistants are moving from information layer to transaction layer — fast.

A Conference Board survey of 141 Fortune Global 500 CEOs — conducted May 4 through May 18 — found confidence fell 12 points in Q2 to 47, below the 50 threshold that signals negative sentiment. The Iran conflict is the primary cited factor. But the macro backdrop matters for AI capital allocation: CEOs who lack confidence pull back on investment. AI infrastructure commitments — data centers, GPU clusters, long-term cloud contracts — are multi-year bets. A sustained confidence decline among the largest enterprise buyers could slow the deployment cycle even as model capabilities continue to advance.

On deployments. AWS launched its Agentic Shopping Assistant this Friday, built on Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and OpenSearch. The system draws on infrastructure developed for Alexa for Shopping, which served more than 300 million customers last year and helped generate nearly $12 billion in incremental sales. AWS claims conversational shopping sessions convert at 3.5 times the rate of traditional keyword search. Retailers can deploy customized assistants within weeks. The open question — which AWS has not answered — is how customer conversation data is retained and whether it flows to underlying model providers.

AWS Sales deployed Field Advisor on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate more than 20 domain-specific agents across its global sales organization. Before the deployment, representatives had to manually context-switch between agents handling CRM, meeting scheduling, customer insights, product recommendations, and compliance checks. Field Advisor routes requests to the right specialist agent automatically. The architecture uses isolated execution environments, persistent memory, OAuth-based identity propagation, and built-in observability. The result: sales reps spend more time on customer conversations and less on agent management.

Verizon Connect scaled an agentic AI solution to 100,000 daily users on AWS, processing more than 500 million data points per day across 1.2 million active vehicle subscriptions and 80,000 unique data indicators. Before the deployment, fleet managers hunted for anomalies across fragmented paper logs and reactive spreadsheets. The agentic system dynamically investigates new patterns, asks follow-up questions, and adapts its analysis — replacing manual guesswork with centralized intelligence. The architecture was designed for cost-efficiency at scale, though specific cost-per-insight figures were not disclosed.

PhysicsWallah, India's listed edtech company, reported at its Q4 FY26 earnings call this Friday that its AI models now resolve 90 percent of student queries. The company has 3.5 million students spending two hours daily on its platform, generating billions of training data points. It's building small language models in-house — claiming 5x speed and one-tenth the cost of frontier models for its specific use case. Average revenue per user is less than 4,000 rupees. The company is rolling out Aryabhata 2.0 for math queries and an AI Tutor with persistent memory of past student errors. AI revenue is expected to be material in FY27.

Warp, the developer terminal startup, reports that 90 percent of its internal pull requests are now created with AI agents, and that using its latest model integration cuts tokens per task by 30 percent. Warp uses the model to orchestrate agents across local, cloud, and open-source development workflows through its Oz orchestration layer. The terminal has become the coordination point for multi-agent coding workflows — where commands, context, and agent outputs converge. For enterprise engineering teams evaluating agentic coding infrastructure, Warp's numbers are among the most concrete published benchmarks available.

Starburst Data launched its Enterprise Intelligence Platform at its AI+Datanova event in Miami, including general availability of Aida — an AI assistant that lets business users query distributed enterprise data in natural language. The platform introduces a business context layer that aggregates metadata, business rules, and semantic relationships from catalogs, BI tools, and enterprise applications into a graph structure. The goal: reduce hallucinations from AI models by providing shared ground truth across distributed data environments. Starburst's core insight — that 'churn' means different things to finance, product, and sales — is the kind of semantic fragmentation that breaks most enterprise AI deployments.

Google Cloud unveiled AI Threat Defense this week — a platform that bundles Gemini, Wiz, and DeepMind's Codemender agent to automatically find, assess, and patch security flaws. Wiz, acquired by Google for $32 billion in March 2025, identifies vulnerable systems. Codemender rewrites vulnerable code and generates tests to verify each patch. Google deliberately uses multiple models simultaneously — cheap models for continuous scanning, frontier models for critical systems. The platform targets the growing gap between AI-accelerated attack speed and manual human defense cycles. Patch traceability — which model fixed which flaw — is built in.

Off the radar. A governance paper published Friday on Medianama surfaces a structural failure in enterprise agentic systems that no mainstream outlet has picked up. The argument: AI agents don't retain authority because it was granted — they retain it because the context surrounding the grant never disappears. A finance agent given a bounded mandate to reconcile invoices for a quarterly close can keep reconciling after the mandate expires — not because the token survived, but because the orchestration graph, the warm memory state, and the adjacent agents still treat the reconciliation function as live. Every individual control behaves correctly. The system regenerates the authority anyway. For risk and compliance officers deploying agents in finance workflows, this is not a theoretical problem.

SQLite — one of the most widely deployed software libraries on earth, embedded in billions of devices — added an AGENTS.md file this week and then hardened its language: it removed the word 'currently' from 'SQLite does not accept agentic code,' making the prohibition permanent. The SQLite forum was being flooded with AI-generated bug reports of varying quality, forcing the project to spin up a separate bug forum. Maintainer D. Richard Hipp is resolving issues with a flurry of commits. The signal for enterprise open-source strategy: AI-generated contributions are arriving faster than governance frameworks can handle them, and critical infrastructure projects are drawing hard lines.

The curl project — the networking library underpinning most of the internet's HTTP traffic — is receiving security reports at 4 to 5 times the 2024 rate and double the 2025 rate, per maintainer Daniel Stenberg. More than one credible AI-assisted security report arrives per day. The quality is higher than ever — detailed, long, technically rigorous. Stenberg says his wife has raised concerns about his work hours for the first time. The good news: most vulnerabilities found are rated low or medium severity. The implication for enterprise security teams: AI is dramatically accelerating the discovery of vulnerabilities in the open-source dependencies your stack relies on. Patch cycles need to compress accordingly.

China formally added AI chips to its 'secure and reliable' technology assessment list this week — creating a new certification category for AI training and inference chips. The certifications are valid for three years and function as the de facto procurement catalogue for party agencies, state-owned enterprises, and Xinchuang-covered customers. Beijing is now targeting Nvidia and foreign GPU suppliers directly, after earlier rounds of Xinchuang focused on Intel, AMD, and Oracle. For semiconductor investors and supply chain strategists, this is the clearest signal yet that China's domestic AI chip ecosystem — Huawei, Cambricon, and others — is being formally institutionalized as the alternative to US hardware.

Airbus announced a partnership with Mistral AI this week to develop sovereign AI capabilities for aerospace applications — a deal that received almost no English-language coverage. Mistral, the French AI lab, is positioning itself as the European alternative to US frontier models for defense-adjacent and regulated industries. The Airbus deal is the most concrete signal yet that European aerospace primes are treating AI sovereignty — not just AI capability — as a procurement criterion. For enterprise buyers in regulated sectors across the EU, the Airbus-Mistral partnership is a template: sovereign model provenance is becoming a contract requirement, not just a preference.

Korea's Motif Technologies raised $16.6 million in a Series B this week to advance a homegrown Korean-language AI foundation model. The raise received no coverage in Western tech media. It follows a broader pattern across Asia: Azerbaijan's Azercell built a production-ready Azerbaijani LLM on AWS SageMaker in six weeks, achieving 23 percent higher training throughput and 58 percent lower peak GPU memory usage. The pattern — small, language-specific foundation models built for morphologically complex languages with limited training data — is accelerating across markets that frontier English-centric models underserve. For financial institutions operating in these markets, local-language model capability is becoming a competitive differentiator.

Looking ahead to next week. Anthropic's IPO timeline is the most consequential item to watch. The $65 billion Series H was described by TechCrunch as potentially the company's last private fundraise. Run-rate revenue at $47 billion, a first operating profit expected in Q2, and a valuation approaching $1 trillion all point to an S-1 filing window opening in the second half of 2026. Any signal from Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao — who led the Series H — about filing timing will move the broader AI equity complex. OpenAI's own IPO process runs in parallel, and Anthropic's valuation now sets the reference point.

FinOps X 2026 runs June 8 through 11 in San Diego — and this year it's a market-moving event, not just a practitioner conference. The State of FinOps 2026 Report shows 98 percent of FinOps teams now manage AI spending. The Uber and Microsoft token-shock stories published this Friday will dominate the agenda. Watch for announcements from cloud providers on token cost governance tools, and for enterprise buyers to signal how they're restructuring AI budgets after Q1 overruns. Any new pricing frameworks from AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud announced at or around FinOps X will have immediate implications for AI vendor contract negotiations.

The Illinois AI Safety Measures Act heads to Governor Pritzker's desk next week for signature. OpenAI endorsed it publicly this Friday. Once signed, Illinois joins New York and California in a converging state-level framework that OpenAI itself called a de facto national standard. Enterprise legal and compliance teams should treat the signing as the trigger to audit existing AI deployment contracts against the new transparency, audit, and incident-reporting requirements. The annual third-party audit mandate alone will create a new market for AI compliance services — watch for the first vendor announcements in that space.

Groq's $650 million internal raise — reported Friday by Axios — is expected to close in the coming weeks. The round is effectively guaranteed: backers Disruptive and Infinitium have agreed to fill it if other investors pass. But the strategic question is whether Groq's inference cloud can compete on cost-per-token against AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud at scale. Watch for any customer announcements or inference pricing disclosures from Groq's new leadership team. The Nvidia technology licensing deal from December gives Groq a differentiated chip architecture — the question is whether that translates to a durable margin advantage in a market where token prices are falling fast.

Money20/20 Europe opens next week, with agentic AI in financial infrastructure as the headline theme. The timing is sharp — Liquid's Co-Invest app launched inside ChatGPT and Claude this Friday, Robinhood's Agentic Trading went live this week, and Google Pay published its Universal Commerce Protocol for agent-driven transactions. Expect European financial regulators and bank technology chiefs to respond publicly to the agentic trading wave at the conference. Any regulatory guidance on AI agent authority in financial transactions — particularly around liability when an agent executes a trade without fresh human approval — will be the most consequential output of the week.
